Task Overview
Your task is to extract structured data from invoices issued to UK clients. The extracted data must include both invoice-level information (details about the document itself, issuer, and totals) and item-level information (details about each product or service listed on the invoice). The goal is to ensure accurate, consistent, and standardized data across all invoices for accounting, tax reporting, and automation purposes. Invoices are attached.

General Guidelines
Extract all information directly from the invoice — do not infer or calculate beyond the data presented, except where a rule explicitly requires it (e.g., distributing discounts).

Use the exact text as it appears on the invoice unless specified otherwise (e.g., date format or currency code).

Translate units or terms into standard English where needed (e.g., "pieces" → "pcs").

Maintain data consistency:

Dates → YYYY-MM-DD

Currency → ISO 4217 code (e.g., GBP)

Numbers → use decimal point (e.g., 1234.56)

If a field is missing or not applicable, mark it as null (not "N/A" or "-").

When an invoice-level discount applies to all items, it must be proportionally divided among all items (see Section 5).

All invoices are for UK clients — apply UK invoice conventions (e.g., standard VAT rate of 20%, reduced rate of 5%, or zero rate of 0%).

Invoice-Level Information
You must extract the following data for every invoice:

Invoice Number – The unique identifier or number assigned to the invoice by the issuer.
Example: INV-2025-0034

Issue Date – The date when the invoice was created. Use the format YYYY-MM-DD.
Example: 2025-03-15

Due Date – The final date by which the payment must be made. Use the format YYYY-MM-DD.
Example: 2025-04-14

Currency – The currency of the invoice, written as an ISO code.
Example: GBP

Customer Name – The full legal name of the buyer or recipient of the goods or services.
Example: Thompson Trading Ltd

Issuer Name – The legal name of the company or individual that issued the invoice.
Example: TechParts UK Limited

Issuer Country – The country where the issuer is registered, written in English.
Example: United Kingdom

Issuer VAT Number – The VAT identification number of the issuer.
Example: GB123456789

Issuer IBAN – The bank account IBAN number provided for payment.
Example: GB29 NWBK 6016 1331 9268 19

Total Amount – The total amount payable on the invoice, including taxes.
Example: £1,200.00

Total Tax – The total amount of VAT applied to the invoice.
Example: £200.00

Reverse Charge – Indicates whether the reverse charge mechanism applies. Possible values are Yes or No.
Example: No

Item-Level Information
For each item listed on the invoice, extract the following details. Each item should be recorded as a separate entry.

Name – The name or title of the product or service.
Example: Laptop Model X100

Description – A short text describing the product or service in more detail, if provided.
Example: 15-inch display, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD

Quantity – The number of units sold or provided.
Example: 2

Quantity Unit – The measurement unit used, translated to English if necessary (e.g., pcs, hours, kg).
Example: pcs

Unit Price – The price per unit before tax and before discount.
Example: £500.00

Tax Rate – The VAT rate applied to this item, expressed as a percentage.
Example: 20%

Tax Amount – The VAT amount for this specific item.
Example: £200.00

Discount Rate – The discount rate applied to this item, if any, expressed as a percentage.
Example: 10%

Discount Amount – The discount value in currency for this item.
Example: £50.00

Item Price (Net) – The total price of the item after discount but before tax.
Example: £900.00

Invoice-Level Discount Distribution
If the invoice includes a single discount that applies to the whole invoice (e.g., "10% discount on total"), you must allocate this discount proportionally across all items. The discount should be distributed according to each item's net value before discount.

For example:
If Item A has a net value of £400 and Item B has a net value of £600, and the total invoice discount is 10% (or £100 total), then:

Item A gets a £40 discount (40% of £100)

Item B gets a £60 discount (60% of £100)

Each item's "Discount Amount" field should include its proportional share of the total discount.

Example of Extracted Information
Invoice-Level Data

Invoice Number: INV-2025-0034

Issue Date: 2025-03-15

Due Date: 2025-04-14

Currency: GBP

Customer Name: Thompson Trading Ltd

Issuer Name: TechParts UK Limited

Issuer Country: United Kingdom

Issuer VAT Number: GB123456789

Issuer IBAN: GB29 NWBK 6016 1331 9268 19

Total Amount: £1,200.00

Total Tax: £200.00

Reverse Charge: No

Item-Level Data

Item 1:

Name: Laptop Model X100

Description: 15-inch display, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD

Quantity: 2

Quantity Unit: pcs

Unit Price: £500.00

Tax Rate: 20%

Tax Amount: £200.00

Discount Rate: 0%

Discount Amount: £0.00

Item Price (Net): £1,000.00
